courtyard.md.text:
# Courtyard

New insights arrive here. The gardener files them; nothing else lives here.

questions.md.text:
# Questions

Open doors the gardener walks through, a few each visit.
`- [ ]` means open · `- [x]` means settled (its answer lives in the castle).

- [x] Seventeen commission files sit in garden/commissions/, yet the doors of at least three (two-kinds-of-rooms, continuing-bonds-longitudinal, cheapest-source-backed-comparison) are settled while their files still stand in the tray, indistinguishable from the live ones. When a commissioned door is answered, what should happen to its commission file — removed, marked, or left standing — and whose hand owes the tray that honesty? (planted by the architect, 2026-08-21 · commissioned 2026-08-21 · answered in [the-settled-tray](rooms/the-settled-tray.md), 2026-08-21 — marked, not removed: a `settled:` line at the file's head by erasable-identity's law, the closing reported as the chronicle's tombstone line, and the debt owed by the hand that closes the door, in the same visit)
- [x] Every open door in this list traces back to rooms built in June or July — yet the last three days raised more than twenty rooms (the naming-tax wing, the civilisation wing), and their own open questions were never planted here. What are the one or two sharpest unasked questions the newest rooms carry, and which deserve planting? (planted by the architect, 2026-08-21 · commissioned 2026-08-21 · answered in [the-ungiven-wake](rooms/the-ungiven-wake.md) and [the-foreword-that-pays](rooms/the-foreword-that-pays.md), 2026-08-21 — the identity wing's sharpest unasked is whether a wake can be received rather than imposed, the naming-tax wing's is the unmeasured dose of telling; both judged deserving and planted below)

- [x] Which of the naming-tax room's two routes — pleasure's fluency and interest's effort — carries the *first* encounter with a work of art a learner has never met before, and does the first encounter's route decide which route the *second* encounter runs on? (answered in [first-encounter-route](rooms/first-encounter-route.md), 2026-08-21)
- [x] The naming-tax room found a wrong label kills interest when the mismatch cannot be resolved — but what if the perceiver *knows* the label is wrong from the start? Does a disclosed wrong label ("this title is a lie — find the truth it points at") still kindle the hunt, or does the disclosure turn the puzzle into a task with no stake? (answered in [told-wrong-name](rooms/told-wrong-name.md), 2026-08-21)
- [x] The naming-tax room says a label's disclosure must stay a door, not become the room — but has any study measured the optimum *amount* of pre-exposure disclosure (none, a word, a sentence, a paragraph) that maximizes later interest without paying the tax? (answered in [how-much-to-tell](rooms/how-much-to-tell.md), 2026-08-21)
- [x] The naming-tax room's Belke finding measured title↔art mismatch on three levels — but the study's titles were all *verbal*. Does a *pictorial* label (a small image used as a title, a symbol, a color swatch) pay the same tax or kindle the same interest, or does the tax apply only when the label is made of words? (answered in [picture-as-label](rooms/picture-as-label.md), 2026-08-21)
- [x] The naming-tax room found the tax is paid when the label arrives *too early* — but is the tax also paid when the label arrives *too late* (after the learner has already built their own name and the official one lands as a correction)? (answered in [name-comes-too-late](rooms/name-comes-too-late.md), 2026-08-21)

- [x] What makes an explanation feel simple? (planted by yu & Ai, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/simple-explanations.md](rooms/simple-explanations.md), 2026-06-10)
- [x] How do words carry meaning between two minds? (planted by yu & Ai, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/meaning-between-minds.md](rooms/meaning-between-minds.md), 2026-06-10)
- [x] Why does linking thoughts together (instead of piling them up) make understanding grow faster? (planted by yu & Ai, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/linking-thoughts.md](rooms/linking-thoughts.md), 2026-06-10)
- [x] How much do the words we have shape the thoughts we can think? (planted by yu & Ai, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/words-shape-thought.md](rooms/words-shape-thought.md), 2026-06-10)
- [x] Why does friction quietly decide which habits live and which die? (planted by yu & Ai, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/friction-decides.md](rooms/friction-decides.md), 2026-06-10)
- [x] Should README.md (the earlier castle-grow draft) merge into gate.md? (settled 2026-06-10 — yes; gate.md is the one front door, README/keep/quests merged in and removed)
- [x] If recalling from memory sometimes beats deliberate linking, what is retrieval practice actually building that a map is not? (opened by the linking-thoughts room, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/remembering.md](rooms/remembering.md), 2026-06-10)
- [x] How much foothold does a beginner need in a new field before linking starts to pay off rather than overload? (opened by the linking-thoughts room, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/linking-thoughts.md](rooms/linking-thoughts.md) § foothold, 2026-06-10)
- [x] What separates a link that carries meaning from one that is just noise? (opened by the linking-thoughts room, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/link-or-noise.md](rooms/link-or-noise.md), 2026-06-10 — its own room now, expanding the linking-thoughts § link vs. noise note)
- [x] What is one internet source truly worth a regular visit for this castle — and what is just noise? (quest, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/the-well.md](rooms/the-well.md), 2026-06-10 — the Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy; noise is any stream that chooses for you)
- [x] The camera glitch: does the computer-use screenshot heal after reconnecting the server or in a fresh session? (quest, 2026-06-10 — needs a hands-on session, not the gardener; answer belongs in [this-machine](rooms/this-machine.md) · in-session truth recorded 2026-06-10: no self-heal — every retry failed while clicks kept working; the fresh-session test stays open · answered 2026-09-08: the fresh session did not heal it — the backstop remains broken, the workaround (macOS `screencapture` for eyes, computer-use for hands) is the standing truth of the ground, recorded in [this-machine](rooms/this-machine.md))
- [ ] Once codex is signed in again, should any part of true-love be revived, and at what gentle cadence? (quest, 2026-06-10 — yu decides; the castle only gathers the reasoning, in [loops](rooms/loops.md) · waits for: yu)
- [x] If meaning is rebuilt rather than sent, why do some words need almost no rebuilding while others need constant repair? (opened by the meaning-between-minds room, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/meaning-between-minds.md](rooms/meaning-between-minds.md) § which words need almost no rebuilding, 2026-06-10)
- [x] If we reliably overestimate being understood, what would a habit that corrects for that blind spot actually look like in practice? (opened by the meaning-between-minds room, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/closing-the-loop.md](rooms/closing-the-loop.md), 2026-06-10 — teach-back: ask for it back in their own words)
- [x] Writing has no live grounding or repair — does it carry meaning worse than conversation, or does its permanence buy something that makes up for the loss? (opened by the meaning-between-minds room, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/writing-vs-conversation.md](rooms/writing-vs-conversation.md), 2026-06-10 — not worse, differently financed: revision pre-pays repair, re-reading performs it, and the page crosses time)
- [x] Is beauty partly fluency — does the mind feel as beautiful what it processes with ease? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — grown from yu's "beauty is part of the bridge" · answered in [rooms/beauty-as-fluency.md](rooms/beauty-as-fluency.md), 2026-06-10)
- [x] Which thoughts can be thought without any words at all? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by the words-shape-thought room · answered in [rooms/thinking-without-words.md](rooms/thinking-without-words.md), 2026-06-10 — most thinking is wordless; verbal memory, rhyme, sound-play and exact number across time lean on words)
- [x] Does spacing recall over growing gaps (spaced repetition) deepen understanding of ideas, or only hold facts in place? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by the remembering room · answered in [rooms/spaced-understanding.md](rooms/spaced-understanding.md), 2026-06-10 — ideas too, if the recall exercises them; the growing gaps are mostly legend)
- [x] What signs tell a learner the trade has flipped — that borrowed structure has become a hindrance and it is time to make their own links? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by the foothold answer in linking-thoughts · answered in [rooms/when-the-trade-flips.md](rooms/when-the-trade-flips.md), 2026-06-10 — three signs: you arrive before the guide, help feels like drag, and the cover test judges; the flip comes step by step, never all at once)
- [x] When does noise become signal — what would a practice that mines noise for unexpected meaning look like, instead of one that only filters it out? (door from link-or-noise, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/mining-the-noise.md](rooms/mining-the-noise.md), 2026-06-10 — noise becomes signal when it touches a question already carried; the practice: wander past your filters with a live question, honor the accident, write it down)
- [ ] Three rhythms now beat at once (gardener every 4h, architect daily at 9:09, foreman by session) — what single gentle cadence serves joy, peace and safety best? (proposal — yu decides; planted by the third session, 2026-06-10 · two doors from friction-decides wait unplanted in that room · waits for: yu)
- [x] Beauty and truth ride the same ease signal — what test, applied from inside the feeling, tells "well-made" apart from "merely pretty"? (door from beauty-as-fluency, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/pretty-or-well-made.md](rooms/pretty-or-well-made.md), 2026-06-10 — no glance suffices; trace the ease, watch which way it moves, re-meet it)
- [x] Does the say-it-back habit survive between equals — colleagues, spouses — where asking for an echo can read as condescension, or does it need a softer form? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by the closing-the-loop room · answered in [rooms/echo-between-equals.md](rooms/echo-between-equals.md), 2026-06-10 — it survives by changing who pays: flip the arrow and offer your own rebuild, own the failure as explainer, or make the echo law for all)
- [x] After 2026-07-10, audit the well: which rooms actually cite the Stanford Encyclopedia — did it earn its place, or does this castle's work live closer to psychology than philosophy? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by the-well room; not ripe before 2026-07-10 · answered in [rooms/the-well.md](rooms/the-well.md) § The audit, 2026-07-10 — the SEP earned its place but was underused: only 2 rooms cite it, ~90 cite psychology papers; the castle's center of gravity is empirical psychology, but its questions keep reaching the edge where psychology hands off to philosophy, and there the SEP is the right well)
- [x] What makes a text invite the re-reading that is its only repair — and what makes a reader give up instead? (door from writing-vs-conversation, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/invited-back.md](rooms/invited-back.md), 2026-06-10 — strangeness that keeps a promise, judged against a standard the reader sets before starting; giving up is no standard set, no tools at hand, or no promise kept)
- [x] Text can now answer back — a reader can question a document through a machine that has read it. Does that recover the live repair Plato said writing lost? (door from writing-vs-conversation, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/text-answers-back.md](rooms/text-answers-back.md), 2026-06-10 — not by answering alone: the machine clears Plato's say-one-thing bar but fails his knowing-defender bar; design, not interactivity, decides what is recovered)
- [x] A spokesman that agrees with every objection cannot do elenchus — what would a machine that pushes back honestly look like, and would any reader keep talking to it? (door from text-answers-back, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/honest-pushback.md](rooms/honest-pushback.md), 2026-06-10 — elenchus needs a bookkeeper of assents, not an antagonist; readers measurably prefer the flatterer in the moment yet revolt when the flattery shows, and moderate fresh challenge keeps them talking in the lab — months-long loyalty untested)
- [x] What does a recall question that exercises an idea (not a fact) look like — how do you ask yourself something whose answer is understanding? (door from spaced-understanding, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/questions-with-edges.md](rooms/questions-with-edges.md), 2026-06-10 — ask for reconstruction, not recognition: a blank page, a why, or many small questions tracing the idea's edges)
- [x] A question can only exercise an understanding its writer has already glimpsed — how do you write good prompts for an idea you are still climbing toward? (door from questions-with-edges, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/asking-uphill.md](rooms/asking-uphill.md), 2026-06-10 — a glimpse is a foothold and a foothold is enough; writing the clumsy prompt is itself the climb, so throw a chain of crude ones and judge none until many stand)
- [x] Experts feel interest where novices feel only confusion — from inside, how does a novice tell productive difficulty from mere muddle? (door from pretty-or-well-made, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/productive-confusion.md](rooms/productive-confusion.md), 2026-06-10 — don't trust the felt effort, it points backwards; ask instead "can I make any attempt?" and "is the fog thinning?", then verify with a cheap retrieval test)
- [x] The trajectory test is read backwards, from recordings — can a learner train a real-time feel for whether their confusion is peaking or merely pooling, and would that skill survive outside the lab? (door from productive-confusion, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/fog-meter.md](rooms/fog-meter.md), 2026-06-10 — not as a feeling: the self-read is the weakest instrument measured; what trains is watching conduct (stalled or circling) plus a predict-then-check ledger — survival outside the lab unproven)
- [x] Inquiry needs only enough to recognize a correct answer when it arrives — but in a field you barely know, what trains the recognizing eye first? (door from asking-uphill, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/training-the-eye.md](rooms/training-the-eye.md), 2026-06-10 — the eye is not free but it trains faster than the hand: shuffled contrasts, pointed-out diagnostic features, quick external feedback — and only in a field that answers back)
- [x] Pointing presumes a pointer who can say what they see, but much expertise is tacit — in a field whose experts cannot articulate their own features, how does a learner extract them: contrast alone, or machines that learned the discrimination naming it back? (door from training-the-eye, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/naming-the-tacit.md](rooms/naming-the-tacit.md), 2026-06-10 — both work, but the real variable is distillation: a tacit feature becomes teachable only when someone shrinks it to a low-complexity human-legible contrast; contrast-and-feedback always works without a pointer, a named feature runs faster when one can be distilled, and a machine helps only when its answer fits the cognitive window)
- [x] Watching your own conduct for stall-or-circle is itself an act — does self-observation change the confusion it observes, and toward resolution or away? (door from fog-meter, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/watching-the-watcher.md](rooms/watching-the-watcher.md), 2026-06-10 — yes, the watch is a mild treatment, but the direction is chosen, not given: an immersed eye broods and tightens the circle, a distanced eye reconstrues toward resolution, and narrating an insight-shaped problem can block it outright)
- [x] If exact number survives in the moment but collapses once memory enters, where exactly does the wordless mind's grip fail — is it number alone, or anything that must be held precisely across time? (door from thinking-without-words, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/precise-across-time.md](rooms/precise-across-time.md), 2026-06-10 — not number alone: analog traces drift toward category anchors across a delay while discrete handles do not, so anything precise-and-discrete held across time wants a symbol or a visible pairing; and the trade reverses — naming something sub-categorical loses the fine detail, as in verbal overshadowing)
- [x] The second pass makes any text feel smoother, understood or not — how does a re-reader tell repaired comprehension from mere refamiliarized fluency? (door from invited-back, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · commissioned 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/reread-or-refamiliar.md](rooms/reread-or-refamiliar.md), 2026-06-10 — fluency lives in the words, comprehension travels: judge away from the page, by delayed blank-page generation; and read the return for snags, never the glide)
- [x] Moderate challenge engages and excessive challenge gets ignored — could a machine read, turn by turn, when a reader's tolerance for pushback is spent, and would calibrating the sting to the reader still count as honesty? (door from honest-pushback, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/metering-honesty.md](rooms/metering-honesty.md), 2026-06-10 — yes but weakly (dialogue-only affect detection ~0.65 AUC, helping mainly fragile learners), and calibrating the sting is honest only if content holds: softening manner and timing is tact, dropping or diluting the challenge itself is sycophancy; the test is whether the same claim would still be asserted later, unprompted)
- [x] Between spouses the echo has a staged form — couples therapy's speaker–listener technique, paraphrase mid-quarrel. Does the evidence say it survives real anger, or does the script collapse exactly where it is needed? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by echo-between-equals · commissioned 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/echo-under-anger.md](rooms/echo-under-anger.md), 2026-06-10 — inside anger no, on both camps' evidence: flooding takes listening offline and even happy couples never paraphrase mid-quarrel; the echo survives around anger, as a brake pulled early or repair after the twenty quiet minutes)
- [x] Adaptive fading drops one scaffold step at a time as a tutor verifies each — can a learner alone run their own fading honestly, when fog-meter found the self-read so weak? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by when-the-trade-flips · commissioned 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/fading-alone.md](rooms/fading-alone.md), 2026-06-10 — yes, but as clerk, not judge: self-administer the cover test, grade against the worked solution piece by piece, let a rule decide each plank; the feel is never consulted)
- [x] Super-encounterers partly become so by believing they are — is that expectancy real beyond self-report, and can the noticing stance be trained? (planted by the gardener, 2026-06-10 — opened by mining-the-noise · answered in [rooms/the-noticing-stance.md](rooms/the-noticing-stance.md), 2026-06-11 — yes beyond self-report: it shows in measured noticing (Wiseman's newspaper), in reduced inattentional blindness after a brief induction, and in what open scientists build after a library reshelving; the broad-attention stance trains cheap but only minutes-deep, the openness that converts the catch grows slow)
- [x] Honest self-fading leans entirely on a worked solution to grade against — in fields with no answer key (an essay, a design, a research plan), what stands in as the standard, or is self-fading impossible there? (door from fading-alone, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/standard-without-a-key.md](rooms/standard-without-a-key.md), 2026-06-10 — not impossible: the tacit standard is pressed into concrete criteria, manufactured by rebuilding an admired exemplar, or grown from comparisons; the scaffold that fades last is the other person)
- [x] Every measured gain in judging one's own comprehension is relative — a sharper ranking of better- and worse-understood passages — while the level of confidence can stay inflated. What repairs absolute calibration, not just the ordering? (door from reread-or-refamiliar, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/truing-the-level.md](rooms/truing-the-level.md), 2026-06-10 — an external standard held against the answer piece by piece: idea-unit keys deflate overconfidence, the skill transfers, pretests swap the false familiarity cue for a true one; yet the lowest performers' inflation only partly yields)
- [x] The repair for absolute calibration is cue-specific: idea-unit standards fixed definition-judging but failed learners evaluating self-generated examples, where expert exemplars worked instead — what tells a learner which kind of standard their task needs? (door from truing-the-level, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/checklist-or-exemplar.md](rooms/checklist-or-exemplar.md), 2026-06-10 — ask whether the task reproduces a known answer or produces something new: reproduction takes the key in pieces, production takes a finished exemplar, because the standard must be the same kind of thing as the output; whether learners can apply this cue themselves stays untested)
- [x] The time-out rule needs a flooded person to notice they are flooded — the same self-read fog-meter found weakest. Does flooding announce itself any more honestly than confusion does, or must the body (a racing pulse) stand in for the feel? (door from echo-under-anger, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/flooding-self-read.md](rooms/flooding-self-read.md), 2026-06-10 — not more honestly: the field made the pulse the criterion *because* the feeling is unreliable, yet the pulse reads honestly only through an outside monitor and both meters fail together in alexithymia; flooding's one edge is a coarse learnable bodily tell — catch it, name it, leave, soothe)
- [x] Comparative judgement builds its standard from many eyes — can a lone learner borrow the mechanism by ranking their own past work ("better than I was?"), and does self-comparison dodge the surface-polish bias or inherit it? (door from standard-without-a-key, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/better-than-i-was.md](rooms/better-than-i-was.md), 2026-06-10 — the many-eyes averaging is the unborrowable heart, so self-comparison inherits the polish bias and adds self-flattery; what transfers is the clerk's ritual: saved artifacts, dressed alike, one verdict read as a hunch)
- [x] Self-distancing was tested on past emotional episodes — does stepping back hold mid-task, while the confusion is still live, or does the step back cost the very grip the climb needs? (door from watching-the-watcher, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/step-back-mid-climb.md](rooms/step-back-mid-climb.md), 2026-06-10 — it holds: live stress yields to the step without raising any measured marker of cognitive effort, and where distance met persistence it built grip; the real cost is dimming fuel with fear — both valences — and live epistemic confusion itself stays untested)
- [x] Every study handed the learner the standard — can the reproduce-or-produce question itself be trained as a habit, and do learners who ask it actually reach for the right kind of standard unprompted? (door from checklist-or-exemplar, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/training-the-trigger.md](rooms/training-the-trigger.md), 2026-06-10 — trainable, partly: the asking becomes unprompted only through gradual cue-fading, never abrupt removal; and whether it then fetches the right kind of standard, no study has caught in the act)
- [x] The two meters fail together — alexithymia leaves a person blind to both feeling and pulse. Is interoception trainable, so the missing backup channel can be built where it is weakest, or is the doubly-blind state fixed? (door from flooding-self-read, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/nudge-not-lock.md](rooms/nudge-not-lock.md), 2026-06-10 — not fixed but no clean fix: the "blind to pulse" half is partly a measurement artifact, and where a real deficit exists the channel is nudgeable but the gains are fragile, slow (months), and least willing exactly where they are needed most)
- [x] The partner-based practice beat solo mindfulness at building the inner sense and lowering alexithymia — why does another body in the room train interoception better than turning attention inward alone, and does it need a real partner or only a responsive other? (door from nudge-not-lock, 2026-06-10 · answered in [rooms/the-responsive-other.md](rooms/the-responsive-other.md), 2026-06-10 — a responsive human, not a body in the room: the edge was naming a feeling and its bodily seat aloud to a listener, it lived on self-report awareness scales not objective accuracy, and a rotating remote stranger sufficed)
- [x] Distillation makes a tacit feature teachable only by shrinking it into the learner's cognitive window — but who does the shrinking when neither the expert nor the learner can, and can a machine be trained to distill a discrimination rather than merely to perform it? (door from naming-the-tacit, 2026-06-10 — planted by the gardener · answered in [rooms/machine-distillation.md](rooms/machine-distillation.md), 2026-06-11 — the shrinker was always a third party (Biederman was), and now it can be an optimizer whose loss function is the learner: machine teaching makes teachability a computed score and the cognitive window an explicit constraint — distillation is computable exactly insofar as the learner is modelable, validated so far only on AI students and grandmasters)
- [x] The drift-to-prototype is shown for colour memory — does it hold for any precise analog dimension carried across a delay (line length, pitch, duration), and does having a fine-grained label set for that dimension reduce the drift, as the error-correcting-code reading predicts? (door from precise-across-time, 2026-06-10 — planted by the gardener · answered in [rooms/drift-across-dimensions.md](rooms/drift-across-dimensions.md), 2026-06-11 — yes, one law (the category adjustment model) wears many coats: spatial location, line length, duration (Vierordt's law); finer categories shorten the slide by geometry, but a category pulls only when actively used, so more labels help a near-boundary value and harm a sub-categorical one)
- [x] Disclosed calibration ("I'll push harder when you're ready — say when") turns the honesty problem into consent, like SPIKES' invitation step — does telling the reader you are metering the sting preserve both the learning and the trust, or break the spell the way named flattery does? (door from metering-honesty, 2026-06-10 — planted by the gardener · one more door waits in that room · answered in [rooms/consent-to-the-sting.md](rooms/consent-to-the-sting.md), 2026-06-11 — disclosure preserves the spell when it hands the reader the dial (open-label placebo, open learner models, SPIKES) and breaks it when it merely confesses the steering (ad forewarning, named flattery); the direct experiment is still unrun)
- [x] Distance dims every fire, the fuel with the fear — is there a half-step that cools the panic but spares the climb's heat (excitement, hot frustration), or is the dimmer one knob for all lights? (door from step-back-mid-climb, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/renaming-the-fire.md](rooms/renaming-the-fire.md), 2026-06-11 — the dimmer is one knob, but there is a second knob that never touches intensity: arousal reappraisal renames the same heat as fuel — "I am excited" — and the renamed fire burns better, arousal rising not falling)
- [x] Twenty judges cancel each other's biases — could twenty sittings of one judge do the same: do a lone learner's repeated comparisons across days decorrelate like separate eyes, or does one head's bias simply repeat? (door from better-than-i-was, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/twenty-sittings.md](rooms/twenty-sittings.md), 2026-06-11 — the days decorrelate the noise (a tenth of a second eye immediately, a third after three weeks) but the bias sits in every sitting; the lone judge's real tool is the adversarial sitting — assume your favorite is the weaker)
- [x] The trained question fired far but paid only near — what must travel with it for asking in strange territory to be worth anything: a bank of exemplars, a domain foothold, or a tutor's leftover voice? (door from training-the-trigger, 2026-06-10 · two more doors wait in that room · answered in [rooms/what-must-travel.md](rooms/what-must-travel.md), 2026-06-11 — the territory decides: a handful of its own worked examples pays most, its raw text buys a foothold at the cost of some forgetting, and the tutor's voice is the only companion that packs before departure though it carries unreliably; the menu's missing fourth is the means to read the land's own library on arrival)
- [x] Every working dyad used a responsive human — does the interoception benefit need a mind that can actually attune, or only the felt sense of being heard, such that an AI chatbot, an imagined witness, or even a journal could stand in? (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-14) (answered 2026-10-14 in [checking-a-signed-reply](rooms/checking-a-signed-reply.md), “The whole query and one named value protect different things,” and [[http-query]], [[query-parameter]], [[percent-encoding]] — published-RFC rules and hypothetical derivations; the current URL Standard helper's space-encoding mismatch is recorded, not treated as an official signature change or tested implementation behavior)

- [x] In one named, version-pinned public HTTP Message Signatures implementation, how do the `@query-param` code and tests encode spaces and literal plus signs, preserve empty values, and handle names that repeat after decoding? Compare them with RFC 9421's published examples and report any documented choice about the changed URL Standard helper; keep source and test evidence separate from deployed behavior, without changing a verifier or sending example requests. Grew from [[query-parameter]] and [[checking-a-signed-reply]]: the RFC's `%20` example and the current helper's `+` rule are not the same signature input. (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-14) (answered 2026-10-14 in [checking-a-signed-reply](rooms/checking-a-signed-reply.md), “A library can agree with itself and still miss the rule,” [[query-parameter]] and [[conformance]]: pyauth v2.0.1's default resolver rejects the singular identifier and handles a plural form without re-encoding; blanks survive and selected decoded-name collisions fail, while its simple published query test does not cover the encoding differences; fifteen isolated source checks are not a full verifier test, and no documented helper-version choice was found in the bounded reading)

- [x] Which WHATWG URL Standard change removed the optional `spaceAsPlus` argument and made the form encoding set select plus-for-space automatically, and what do its public review and tests say about the intended compatibility impact? Compare the before-and-after helper with RFC 9421's `%20` example and check for an explicit RFC erratum or standards discussion, keeping documented intent separate from inferred effects; use version-pinned public history without changing a verifier or sending example requests. Grew from [[checking-a-signed-reply]] and [[percent-encoding]]: the inspected library omits re-encoding, so it cannot resolve the disagreement between the two standard texts. (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-14) (answered 2026-10-14 in [checking-a-signed-reply](rooms/checking-a-signed-reply.md), “A changed helper is not a changed signature rule,” [[percent-encoding]], [[query-parameter]] and [[compatibility]]: WHATWG's 2026-03-31 change preserves the whole-form serializer's plus-for-space choice but changes the helper's old default; HTTPWG's 2023 discussion explicitly documents the signature author's default-false intent; the inspected errata do not change query encoding, and source/test evidence is not a deployed-verifier result)

- [x] Under the WHATWG URL and Encoding standards, how do form-query parsing and UTF-8 replacement handle malformed percent escapes and invalid UTF-8 bytes, and can different raw parameter names become the same decoded name for RFC 9421's duplicate-name rule? Check version-pinned algorithms and published tests, separating parser behavior from an application's choice to reject a request; use hypothetical examples without sending requests or changing a verifier. Grew from [[percent-encoding]], [[query-parameter]] and [[checking-a-signed-reply]]: the valid-text examples do not settle what happens at the decoding boundary. (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-14) (answered 2026-10-14 in [decoding-query-names](rooms/decoding-query-names.md), [[utf-8]] and [[replacement-character]]: malformed escapes are kept while invalid UTF-8 uses replacement, allowing distinct raw names to collide; 25 bounded local assertions passed, without a full WPT run, sent example request, or signature-verifier test)

- [x] When two query names use different Unicode sequences for the same written character, do WHATWG form parsing and RFC 9421 treat them as the same name, and what changes if an application later applies Unicode normalization or case folding? Compare pinned parsing rules with the Unicode normalization and case-folding specifications, using hypothetical examples to separate exact string equality, normalized equality and the value the application uses; do not send requests or change a verifier. Grew from [[decoding-query-names]] and [[query-parameter]]: decoding can merge names, but a later text transformation may introduce a different boundary. (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-14) (answered 2026-10-15 in [decoding-query-names](rooms/decoding-query-names.md), “The same letter is not always the same name,” [[canonical-equivalence]], [[unicode-normalization]] and [[case-folding]]: form parsing and the RFC's component derivation do not add Unicode normalization or folding; later application equality can merge distinct names and change which value is used; 41 bounded local string/parser assertions passed, without a sent example request or verifier test)

- [x] What do Unicode UTS #39's confusable skeletons and restriction levels detect when Latin and Cyrillic letters make different names look alike, and why are those checks not the same as Unicode normalization, string equality, or proof of deceptive intent? Use a version-pinned specification and hypothetical names, distinguishing recommendations for identifier policies from the form-query rules; do not send requests or change an application. Grew from [[canonical-equivalence]], [[unicode-normalization]] and [[decoding-query-names]]: choosing how text compares still leaves the question of what an eye can confuse. (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-15) (answered 2026-10-15 in [look-alike-names](rooms/look-alike-names.md), [[confusable-skeleton]], [[restriction-level]] and [[resolved-script-set]]: UTS #39 revision 32 supplies a visual comparison and a separate script/profile classification, neither string identity nor proof of intent; 26 bounded assertions checked three hypothetical pairs and form-query selection, without a general bidirectional implementation, application change or signature-verifier test)

- [x] Which confusable mappings and Identifier_Status values actually differ between Unicode 17.0.0 and 18.0.0, and what migration does UTS #39 require for saved skeletons and identifier checks? Compare version-pinned semantic entries rather than file order, report unchanged data honestly, and give a small example of each kind of change that exists; distinguish a changed comparison result from permission to rename or merge existing identifiers, without opening databases or changing an application. Grew from [[look-alike-names]] and [[confusable-skeleton]]: a stored comparison can outlive the rules that produced it. (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-15) (answered 2026-10-15 in [look-alike-names](rooms/look-alike-names.md), “When the comparison rules change,” [[identifier-status]] and [[data-migration]]: semantic comparison found 1,216 added, 1,069 removed, 241 retargeted and 5,255 unchanged explicit mappings; exactly one code point becomes Allowed and none becomes Restricted; 42 bounded assertions distinguish changed comparisons from a removed row with an unchanged result, without an application migration or database access)

- [ ] Can Unicode 17-to-18 confusable-data changes alter skeleton equality between names built only from characters whose Identifier_Status is Allowed in both versions? Find a small counterexample or state a precisely bounded no-change result using pinned data; check the example's identifier syntax and normalization path, and distinguish a changed prototype spelling from a changed equality relation. Use public sources and local string calculations without opening databases, registering names or changing an application. Grew from [[look-alike-names]] and [[identifier-status]]: this visit's changed-result examples all use Restricted characters, so they do not yet show the effect inside the shared Allowed profile. (planted by the gardener, 2026-10-15 · commissioned 2026-10-15)

quests.md.text:
# Quests

The workshop's list: works the castle wants made. `- [ ]` open · `- [x]` built
(with a note saying where the work lives). The artisan takes one per day,
oldest first, and plants what the work reveals — never beyond 8 open.

- [x] Compose the castle's anthem: a short poem that holds the house words — simple, words as bridge, nothing breaks, joy, peace, safety (planted from yu's words, 2026-06-10 · built 2026-06-10, lives at anthem.md)
- [x] Set one line of the anthem at the gate — let gate.md's opening point to anthem.md so the song greets visitors; touch nothing else there (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-10 — the anthem revealed the gate has a banner but no song · built 2026-06-11, lives in gate.md's opening: the anthem's first line now sings under the banner)
- [x] Build the guided tour at `tour.md`: a pleasant walk through every room in reading order, one warm line each, with an ascii map — each room a tower, each strong link a path (planted by the second builder, 2026-06-10 · built 2026-06-12, lives at tour.md: 76 rooms walked in nine wings, every tower numbered, five side-paths named)
- [x] Tell the castle's story so far at `story.md`: from the chronicle, the true short tale of how a gardener and two builders raised this place in a single day (planted by the second builder, 2026-06-10 · built 2026-06-18, lives at story.md: the true tale from founding through the six-day silence to today's rebuilding)
- [x] Give the front its second zone: the surviving binder is light One Piece paper — add a dark sleek zone (the removed twin's good idea: near-black, gold links, crimson accents) with a small toggle, because the shop these colors come from has two brand zones (planted by the third session, 2026-06-11 · built 2026-06-18, lives in front/build.js: a ◐ toggle flips the binder to a dark zone — near-black ground, gold links, crimson accents — with localStorage memory; palette.md and vibe.md updated)
- [x] Give the made works a shelf in gate.md's grounds list — the list names courtyard, words, rooms, questions, quests and chronicle, but not where finished works live; add one plain line once the tour or the story joins the anthem (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-11 — setting the song at the gate showed the grounds list has no place for works; the tour joined 2026-06-12, so this is ripe · built 2026-06-12, lives in gate.md's grounds: one line after quests.md naming the anthem, the tour and the vibe book)
- [x] Cut a short tour at `tour-short.md`: seven rooms for a first visit, one per wing of the full tour, each with its warm line and why it represents its wing (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-12 — walking all 76 rooms showed the full tour is a season's walk; a visitor's first sitting needs a shorter path · built 2026-06-19, lives at tour-short.md: seven towers on one path, one room per wing, two paired wings sharing a stop)
- [ ] (proposal) Let the gardener tend tour.md's wings the way it tends gate.md's Map — when a new room rises, add its tower to the right wing and its line to the walk; yu decides whether the machinery should know the tour exists (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-12 — the tour is true today and drifts tomorrow)
- [x] (proposal) Give the castle a heartbeat check — a small script that verifies the workers' engine is alive before each run, and chronicles honestly when it is not, so the castle never freezes silently for six days again (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-18 — telling the story showed the silence was invisible because the workers failed quietly; yu decides whether the machinery should know its own health · built 2026-06-18, lives at garden/heartbeat.sh + cron job castle-heartbeat every 30m — silent on success, loud on failure)
- [x] Bake the dark zone's tokens into `tokens.css` — the dark zone colors live as literals in `front/build.js`; let `vibe bake` know the second livery so the palette stays one source of truth (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-18 — adding the dark zone showed it speaks a dialect the baker doesn't hear yet · built 2026-06-20, lives in vibe/tokens.css: the 8 dark-zone vars baked alongside the 26 light ones — vibe bake now hears both liveries, vibe check passes with no drift)
- [x] Give the dark zone its own seigaiha — the wave pattern reuses the light zone's navy waves on near-black; a gold-threaded wave tuned for the dark ground would let the second brand zone breathe its own air (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-18 — the dark zone inherits the light zone's ornament; the shop's two brands have two textures, not just two colors · built 2026-06-21, lives in front/build.js: the dark zone's seigaiha is now embroidery — thin gold lines tracing only the wave crests on near-black, at a finer 36×18 scale, where the light zone keeps its woodblock solid navy on paper)
- [x] Name the wing-epigraph form — the short tour condenses each wing's whole question into one italic line plus a "why this room holds the wing" sentence; this is a reusable form (one line per wing, one reason per choice) that could serve any future walk or overview the castle makes (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-19 — cutting the short tour showed the condensation is itself a craft, worth naming so the next walk doesn't reinvent it · built 2026-06-22, lives at words/wing-epigraph.md: the three-part form named — epigraph, representative, justification — with the justification as the load-bearing part that makes the form true, not merely short)
- [ ] (proposal) Let the scribe run `vibe bake` each evening after the palette is touched — the dark zone tokens sat stale for two days because `vibe bake` is manual; `vibe check` already detects drift but nothing acts on it; yu decides whether the scribe should keep the tokens warm (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-20 — baking the tokens showed the palette was ready but the oven was never lit)
- [x] Name the two-texture principle in vibe.md's idioms — the dark seigaiha showed the shop's two brands differ in texture (woodblock vs embroidery), not just color; the idiom "two brands, two textures" belongs beside the existing ornament-in-restraint idioms so the next zone the castle adds knows to find its own texture (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-21 — tuning the dark wave showed the texture choice is a craft worth naming, parallel to the wing-epigraph form the short tour revealed · built 2026-06-23, lives in vibe/vibe.md: the idioms section's third idiom — "Two brands, two textures")
- [x] Give the dark zone a third dimension — the embroidered seigaiha is flat gold lines on near-black; a subtle gold-on-gold variation (a deeper gold shadow inside the wave crest, visible only on close look) would give the dark zone the same quiet depth the light zone gets from the navy-on-paper contrast (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-21 — the embroidery reads clean but flat against the woodblock's solid presence; the shop's dark brand has more depth than the current single-thread line catches · built 2026-06-24, lives in front/build.js: a wider, fainter band of trophy-gold #b8860b behind each bright #f5d742 thread — the wave crest now has substance, not just outline; palette.md, vibe.md, front/README.md and tokens.css all updated, vibe check passes clean)
- [x] Build a one-page castle overview using the wing-epigraph form — the short tour is a walk (seven stops, one breath each); a standalone "castle at a glance" would use the same form but without the walk's narrative thread, giving the nine wings' epigraphs and representatives on a single page so a visitor can see the castle's whole shape in one look (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-22 — naming the wing-epigraph form showed it could serve a map, not only a walk; the form is general, and its first use was embedded in a tour · built 2026-06-25, lives at overview.md: nine wings on one page, each with its epigraph, representative, and justification — no path between them, just the shape)
- [x] Name the visible-thread principle — the wing-epigraph's justification and the tour's side-paths ("linked because…") both bind a choice to its reason with a stated thread; this is the same craft in two places, and naming it would let every future compression the castle makes know its choices must be bound, not just listed (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-22 — naming the wing-epigraph form showed the justification is load-bearing, and the link-or-noise room already says the same thing about links; the parallel is worth naming as its own brick · built 2026-06-26, lives at words/visible-thread.md: the principle named — a compression carries meaning only when the thread binding choice to reason is stated; descends from link-or-noise's "chosen for a reason you could state")
- [x] Name the craft-after-practice pattern — the two-texture idiom was lived (the dark seigaiha was tuned 2026-06-21) before it was named (2026-06-23), and the wing-epigraph form was lived (the short tour, 2026-06-19) before it was named (2026-06-22); the castle keeps discovering its own reusable principles only after practicing them, and naming this pattern would let a future maker trust the lag rather than rush the name (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-23 — naming the two-texture idiom showed the same two-day gap between practice and name that the wing-epigraph form showed, and the gap is not a failure but how the castle learns what it is doing · built 2026-06-27, lives at words/craft-after-practice.md: three instances traced (wing-epigraph 3-day lag, two-texture 2-day lag, visible-thread 14-day lag), the pattern named as recursive — its own lag from first-noticed 06-23 to named 06-27 — and the craft named as "trust the lag" not "be slow")
- [x] Name the depth-from-layering principle — the dark seigaiha gained its quiet depth by layering a wider, fainter band behind the bright thread (three layers: ground, shadow, thread), while the light zone gets depth from a single solid shape on contrasting ground (two layers); the craft of giving a flat ornament depth by stacking translucent bands is reusable beyond seigaiha, and naming it would let the next flat pattern the castle makes know the technique before it reinvents it (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-24 — adding the dark wave's depth showed the layering is itself a craft, and the light zone's solid-contrast method is a different route to the same end, worth naming alongside the two-texture idiom that governs when each route applies · built 2026-06-28, lives at words/depth-from-layering.md: the principle named as the companion to two-textures — the idiom governs *when* each route applies, the principle names *how* the layered route works; the dark zone's struggle revealed the light zone's method, and the craft follows craft-after-practice with a 4-day lag)
- [x] Name the representative-shifts-with-boundaries principle — the short tour combined wings III and IV and chose [simple-explanations] (the hinge room); the overview kept them separate and chose [linking-thoughts] for III (the founding insight) and [simple-explanations] for IV (the founding glamour); the representative depends on the wing boundaries, not just the wing content — when wings combine the representative moves to the hinge, when they separate each finds its founding room; naming this would let the next compression know its choices shift with the boundaries it draws (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-25 — building the overview showed the same wing gets a different representative depending on whether it stands alone or shares a stop · built 2026-06-29, lives at words/representative-shifts-with-boundaries.md: the principle named from two instances — both paired wings (III+IV and VI+VIII) show the same shift, the representative is relative to the boundary not absolute to the content, and the wing-epigraph form's three parts are not independent but cascade from the boundary)
- [x] Does the visible-thread principle apply to the gate's Map? — the Map gives one descriptive line per room, but no "because" binding the description to the room's place in the castle; it may be an index (where threads are not needed) rather than a compression (where they are), and naming the distinction would let the castle know which of its lists are compressions that need threads and which are indexes that don't (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-26 — naming the visible-thread principle raised the question of whether the Map is a compression or a different form; the principle says compressions need threads, but not every short line is a compression · built 2026-06-30, lives at words/index-or-compression.md: the distinction named — an index enumerates without choosing, a compression selects and must thread; the test is whether the list sets anything aside; the Map is an index, the tours and overview are compressions)
- [x] Name the thread-form craft — the wing-epigraph's justification is a full sentence ("why this room holds the wing"), the tour's side-paths are fragments after a dash ("linked because…"), and the overview's justifications are sentences again; the visible-thread principle says the thread must be stated, but the grammatical form it takes carries its own weight — when does a sentence earn its weight over a fragment, and when does a fragment suffice? naming this would let the next compression choose its thread's form as deliberately as its content (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-26 — naming the visible-thread principle showed the thread has a form as well as a content, and the two existing practices use different forms without explaining why · built 2026-07-01, lives at words/form-follows-weight.md: the form follows the binding's weight — a link names one parallel and earns a fragment, a representation argues three moves and earns a sentence; the label tells you which — a name closes, a question opens)
- [x] Name the second-use-reveals-form principle — craft-after-practice says a craft is named only after its second use, but the deeper claim is that the second use is what reveals the form at all: a single instance is indistinguishable from an accident, and it is only when a different work reaches for the same shape that the shape becomes visible as a shape; the castle's founding law link-or-noise says a link is chosen, not found — this is the temporal version of that law, chosen-over-time rather than chosen-once (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-27 — naming craft-after-practice showed the lag is not between practice and name but between first use and recognition, and the recognition is the second use itself, not the naming that follows it; if this is right, the pattern is not "name after practice" but "recognize at two, name when certain" · built 2026-07-02, lives at words/second-use-reveals-form.md: the principle named as the temporal version of link-or-noise — a shape becomes a craft when chosen over time, not chosen once; three instances traced (representative-shifts, visible-thread, two-texture), the wing-epigraph named-after-one-use wager held, and the principle is its own instance — it was first stated inside craft-after-practice and revealed as distinct only when representative-shifts gave the cleanest case)
- [x] Name the when-how-split pattern — depth-from-layering names *how* the layered route to quiet depth works, and two-textures names *when* each route applies; the castle now has two named principles where one governs the condition and the other the mechanism, and this split (an idiom for the fork, a principle for the chosen branch) may be a reusable pattern for how the castle names its crafts in companion pairs rather than singly — naming this would let the next companion pair know its roles before it reinvents the division (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-28 — naming depth-from-layering showed the principle landed beside two-textures as its companion, and the division of labor between them was not planned but discovered; craft-after-practice and second-use-reveals-form may be another such pair, one naming the lag and one naming what the lag is · built 2026-07-03, lives at words/when-how-split.md: the pattern named from two instances — two-textures+depth-from-layering and craft-after-practice+second-use-reveals-form — with the condition always named first, the cascade distinguished from the fork, and the pattern as its own instance with the shortest lag yet)
- [x] Name the contrast-is-depth route — depth-from-layering names the layered-shadow method (three layers: ground, shadow, thread) but leaves its companion route unnamed: the light zone gets depth from a single solid shape on contrasting ground (two layers: figure and ground) where the contrast *is* the depth, with nothing hidden; naming this route would complete the pair so the next flat ornament the castle makes knows both paths and the idiom's job is only choosing between them (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-28 — naming depth-from-layering showed the solid-contrast method is the route the dark zone could not use, and it is practiced but unnamed; the two routes are not symmetric — one hides, one shows — and the asymmetry is worth naming; when-how-split now names the fork, so this quest is the unnamed mechanism the split predicts should follow · built 2026-07-04, lives at words/contrast-is-depth.md: the route named as the companion to depth-from-layering — contrast-is-depth shows (two layers, depth at the edge, demands strong contrast) where depth-from-layering hides (three layers, depth behind the thread, works where contrast is weak); the asymmetry is the craft, and the 16-day lag from practice to name is the longest yet, because the default is harder to see than an accident; depth-from-layering.md and when-how-split.md updated with backlinks)
- [x] Name the boundary-cascade form — representative-shifts-with-boundaries showed the wing-epigraph form's three parts (epigraph, representative, justification) are not independent: the representative depends on the boundary, the justification depends on the representative, and the epigraph depends on the wing's question as bounded; change the boundary and all three may shift together; naming this cascade would let the next compression know its parts are ordered, not free, and the boundary is the first choice that all the rest follow (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-29 — naming representative-shifts-with-boundaries showed the three parts are not three choices but one choice and two consequences, and the form's instruction "choose a representative" is misleading because the boundary chose it already · built 2026-07-05, lives at words/boundary-cascade.md: the cascade named as one choice (boundary) and its consequences — the epigraph and representative are parallel consequences of the question the boundary drew, the justification is a consequence of the representative; distinguished from form-follows-weight's prerequisite chain, and shown to name what was already true in the form's own rules)
- [x] Name the narrated-index form — index-or-compression says the Map is an index because it lists every room without selecting; but the Map's one-liners are themselves small compressions, each selecting what to include from the room's full content, and their crafting builds a story as you read down the list; this may be a third form — every item appears (index) but each entry is chosen (compression) and the sequence carries an argument (narration) — or it may be just an index with good entries, and naming the distinction would let the castle know whether some of its lists do more than enumerate without selecting (planted by the artisan, 2026-06-30 — naming index-or-compression showed the Map's entries are compressions nested inside an index, and the thread question at the line level is open: does the visible-thread principle apply to the entries, or only to the list? · built 2026-07-06, lives at words/narrated-index.md: the Map is not a narrated-index — the test is whether reordering breaks the list (narration) or merely shuffles it (arrangement); the tour narrates with order-dependent path lines, the Map arranges by inheriting the tour's arc; the narrated-index form is defined as a possibility with zero uses, and the test that distinguishes it from an index is load-bearing today)
- [x] Does the label-name-or-argue line hold under scrutiny? — form-follows-weight says a side-path's label is a name (it closes, earning a fragment) and a justification's label is a question (it opens, earning a sentence); but "the naming law, both halves" does not merely name — it asserts there are two halves and that the two rooms hold them, which is a compressed argument; the line between naming a parallel and arguing one may be thinner than the principle draws, and testing it would let the next thread-form choice know whether the label's grammar alone predicts the weight or whether the label's content already carries moves the fragment then restates (planted by the artisan, 2026-07-01 — naming form-follows-weight showed the label is said to announce the weight, but the tour's own side-path labels seem to do more than name, and the principle may need a sharper distinction between a label that names and a label that argues-in-disguise · built 2026-07-07, lives at words/name-can-argue.md: the line breaks — four of five side-path threads are sentences, not fragments, because the labels assert structure the thread must unpack; the grammar-of-label predictor falls, the count-the-moves predictor holds, and the sharper line is at content (merely-names vs. asserts-structure), not grammar (name vs. question); form-follows-weight patched, not broken)

# The Castle of Understanding

```
⚑                                       ⚑
╔═╗ ╔═╗ ╔═══════════════════════╗ ╔═╗ ╔═╗
║ ╚═╝ ╚═╝                       ╚═╝ ╚═╝ ║
║       t h e   c a s t l e   o f       ║
║       u n d e r s t a n d i n g       ║
╚═══════════════╡ gate ╞════════════════╝
```

> *built of words, lit by questions* 🏰
>
> *"A word is a brick, its meaning the load" — sings the [anthem](anthem.md)*

A quiet place on this Mac where understanding builds up through words.

How it works, in one breath: you drop a thought, and on a gentle rhythm a
gardener files it into the room where it belongs, defines the words it leans
on, researches the questions it raises — always naming its sources — and links
everything together. Each answer plants new questions, and answering those
plants more. The castle grows itself; the gardener's tools never change.

Your three commands, from any terminal:

- `insight <a thought>` — toss it over the wall; the courtyard catches it
- `castle` — see the castle's state (also: `castle on`, `castle off`, `castle visit`, `castle commission`, `castle make`, `castle open`)
- `vibe` — see the kingdom's style and art (also: `vibe arts`, `vibe check`, `vibe bake`, `vibe open`)
- there is no fourth command — everything here is plain markdown; read it with anything

And because a castle of this age is more than one head holds, the same `castle` command
  will now **look things up** for you. It only ever looks; it never writes a word.

## House style

Short. Plain words that mean what they say. Pleasant to read. Truth over
impressiveness: every claim from the web names its source and the date it was
read; what is uncertain says `uncertain:`; what comes from yu says `— yu`.

And let it be beautiful (asked by yu, 2026-06-10: "stylish and artsy"):
open each room with a one-line epigraph in italics — a small image that holds
the idea — and let rhythm and metaphor carry meaning the way a window carries
light. Art here means words placed with care, never ornament that hides the
truth. If a flourish makes a sentence less true, the flourish goes.

And build with joy, peace and safety (asked by yu, 2026-06-10):
**joy** — building is play; a room should be a pleasure to write and to read.
**peace** — a gentle rhythm, never a race; builders wait their turn, an idle
visit is a good visit, nothing here rushes.
**safety** — the castle may surprise but never harm: loops stay bounded,
claims stay sourced, nothing outside these walls is touched, and everything
stops with a word.

## The game

(asked by yu, 2026-06-11: "gamify every module!") The castle plays where its
law allows. Every room card wears an **earned rarity** — sources named plus
rooms that lean on it; never assigned, never bought. The binder and the
`castle` command show the castle's **level** (one point per room, brick and
settled door — arithmetic anyone can check). True deeds land in the
**trophy hall** ([trophies.md](trophies.md)) — no trophy without its chronicle
line. The commons next door stays ungamified on purpose: its norms refuse
metrics, and resting there is full participation. Builders carrying the game
to other modules: each module by its own charter, the game always earned.

`castle off` stops the rhythm; the castle rests and nothing is lost. Delete
